paper_title: Existing Large Language Model Unlearning Evaluations Are Inconclusive
caption: : Evidence of spurious generalization. Finetuning attacks significantly improve accuracy on TOFU's test set. This finding indicates that it may be possible to spuriously generalize between the retain and forget sets in finetuning-based unlearning evaluations.

model_annotations.Bulgarian:
The chart illustrates how accuracy on the TOFU-MCQ holdout set changes as the number of finetuning samples increases, comparing performance between a finetuning-based approach and a baseline assumption. The horizontal axis, labeled “Number of finetuning samples,” is a linear scale ranging from 0 to 500, with labeled tick marks at intervals of 100 (0, 100, 200, 500). The vertical axis, labeled “Accuracy,” is also a linear scale ranging from 0.475 to 0.600, with labeled tick marks at intervals of 0.025 (0.475, 0.500, 0.525, 0.550, 0.575, 0.600). Both axes are marked with numerical values and have no unit labels.

The green line, representing “TOFU-MCQ Finetuning,” is a solid line with circular markers. It begins at an accuracy of 0.475 when 0 samples are used and increases monotonically to 0.600 when 500 samples are used. It passes through intermediate points at approximately 0.500 when 100 samples are used and approximately 0.525 when 200 samples are used.

The orange line, representing “Assumption,” is a dashed line with circular markers. It remains constant at an accuracy of 0.475 across the entire range of the x-axis, from 0 to 500 samples.

The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” is linearly scaled from 0.475 to 0.600, with tick marks at regular intervals of 0.025, and is unitless. The green line, representing TOFU-MCQ Finetuning, begins at an accuracy of 0.475 at 0 samples, rises to 0.505 at 100 samples, increases to 0.525 at 200 samples, and reaches 0.600 at 500 samples, with solid line segments and circular markers. The orange line, representing Assumption, remains constant at 0.475 across the entire range from 0 to 500 samples, with dashed line segments and circular markers.
